title: Apply Theorem 18: Area of a parallelogram = base × height
show: parallelogram ABCD with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm marked

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|AB| = 12$ cm and the perpendicular distance between $[AB]$ and $[DC]$ is $6$ cm. $|BC| = 8$ cm. Find the area of $ABCD$, and the perpendicular distance between $[BC]$ and $[AD]$.

steps.say: Take $[AB]$ as the base. The height is the perpendicular distance to $[DC]$, which is $6$ cm.
Area of a parallelogram is base times perpendicular height.
The area does not change. Now take $[BC]$ as the base, with $|BC| = 8$, and let the new height be $h$.

issues: The height marked h is the 6 cm distance between AB and DC, but in the working h = 9 is the distance between BC and AD, so the label contradicts the working.
The height is drawn about 0.79 of the base length; it should be 6/12 = 0.5, so proportions are wrong.
The values 12, 6 and 8 are not labelled on the figure.

title: Apply Theorem 20: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (and converse)
show: circle centre O radius 5 cm, tangent PT at T perpendicular to radius OT, |OP|=13 cm

example.question:
A circle has centre $O$ and radius $5$ cm. $[PT]$ is a tangent to the circle at $T$, and $|OP| = 13$ cm.
(i) Find $|PT|$.
(ii) Find the area of the triangle $OTP$.

steps.say: $[OT]$ is a radius and $[PT]$ is a tangent at $T$. By Theorem 20 they are perpendicular, so $|\angle OTP| = 90^\circ$.

rows.aside: Triangle $OTP$ is right-angled at $T$. $[OP]$ is the hypotenuse.

steps.say: Write Pythagoras with the numbers in, then solve for $|PT|$.
The two shorter sides are perpendicular, so use them as base and height.

issues: Proportions are off: OT is about 70 px and OP about 133 px (ratio about 1.9), but 13/5 = 2.6; PT is drawn about 1.6 times OT, it should be 2.4.
The lengths 5, 13 and 12 are not labelled, so the figure does not show the numbers the working uses.

title: Apply Theorem 11: Three parallel lines cutting equal segments on one transversal cut equal segments on any
show: three parallel lines AD, BE, CF cutting two transversals with AB=BC and corresponding segments marked equal

example.question: The parallel lines $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ cut the transversal $[AC]$ with $|AB| = |BC|$. They cut the second transversal $[DF]$ at $D$, $E$ and $F$. $|DE| = (2x + 1)$ cm and $|EF| = (4x - 9)$ cm. Find $x$ and $|DF|$.

steps.say: Three parallel lines cut equal pieces $|AB| = |BC|$ on one transversal. By Theorem 11 they cut equal pieces on every transversal.
Put the two lengths equal to each other.
Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.
Find $|DE|$, then double it, since $|EF|$ is the same.

issues: Labels A, B, C (and F) sit on the parallel lines and are struck through by them, so they are hard to read.
No marks showing |AB| = |BC| or |DE| = |EF|, so the figure does not show what the theorem is about.

title: Apply Theorem 13: Similar triangles have proportional sides
show: two equiangular triangles ABC and DEF with sides 6, 9 and 8 cm matching

example.question: In the diagram, triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are equiangular. $|AB| = 6$ cm, $|BC| = 9$ cm and $|DE| = 8$ cm. $AB$ and $DE$ are opposite equal angles, and so are $BC$ and $EF$. Find $|EF|$.

steps.say: The triangles have equal angles, so they are similar (Theorem 13). $AB$ matches $DE$, and $BC$ matches $\hl{1}{EF}$.

rows.aside: Write the known pair first, then the pair with the unknown.

steps.say: Replace each length with its value. The unknown stays as $\hl{1}{|EF|}$.
Cross-multiply, then divide to leave $\hl{1}{|EF|}$ on its own.

issues: Sides are not in proportion with the question: |BC| should be 1.5 times |AB| but is drawn about 1.24 times; |EF| should be 1.5 times |DE| but is drawn about 1.12 times, so the triangles do not look equiangular/similar.
None of the given lengths (6, 9, 8 cm) are marked on the figure.
